record.paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Converse of Kuhlmann-Rzepka: characterization of rdr fields via independent defect property
record.original_question: Let (K, v) be a henselian valued field. A finite Galois extension E = (L|K, v) of prime degree p (where p = char Kv) with nontrivial defect (i.e., [L:K] > (vL:vK)[Lv:Kv]) is said to have independent defect if the set Sigma_E = {v(sigma(f)/f - 1) | f in L^x} (for any non-identity sigma in Gal(L|K)) satisfies: Sigma_E = {alpha in vK | alpha > H_E} for some proper convex subgroup H_E of vK such that vK/H_E has no smallest positive element. Otherwise E has dependent defect. The field (K, v) is called an independent defect field if, for some extension of v to K' = K(zeta_p) (a primitive p-th root of unity, or K' = K in characteristic p), all Galois extensions of (K', v) of prime degree p with nontrivial defect have independent defect. A valued field (K, v) is called roughly deeply ramified (rdr) if it satisfies: (DRvp) if char Kv = p > 0, then v(p) is not the smallest positive element of vK; and (DRvr) if char Kv = p > 0, then the completion's O_{K-hat}/pO_{K-hat} is semiperfect. It is proven (Kuhlmann-Rzepka 2023) that every algebraic extension of a roughly deeply ramified field is an independent defect field, and (Rzepka-Szewczyk 2023) that a henselian field is roughly tame (satisfying (TF1r): if char Kv = p > 0 then [-v(p),v(p)] is p-divisible; (TF2): Kv is perfect; (TF3): algebraically maximal) if and only if all its algebraic extensions are defectless fields. By analogy, the conjecture is that a henselian field is roughly deeply ramified if and only if all its algebraic extensions are independent defect fields. Is this conjecture true? That is, if all algebraic extensions of a henselian valued field (K, v) are independent defect fields, does it follow that (K, v) is a roughly deeply ramified field?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let (K, v) be a henselian valued field with value group vK, residue field Kv, and valuation ring O_K. Write p = char Kv when this is positive.

Definitions.

(1) A finite Galois extension (L|K, v) of prime degree p with nontrivial defect (meaning [L:K] > (vL:vK)·[Lv:Kv], so that [L:K] = p, (vL:vK) = 1, and [Lv:Kv] = 1) is said to have independent defect if for some (equivalently, any) non-identity σ ∈ Gal(L|K), the set
   Σ_E := { v(σ(f)/f − 1) : f ∈ L^× , σ(f) ≠ f }
equals { α ∈ vK : α > H_E } for some proper convex subgroup H_E of vK such that the quotient vK/H_E has no smallest positive element. Otherwise E has dependent defect.

(2) The henselian field (K, v) is called an independent defect field if, choosing K' := K(ζ_p) (a primitive p-th root of unity) when char K ≠ p, and K' := K when char K = p, and fixing an extension of v to K', every Galois extension of (K', v) of prime degree p with nontrivial defect has independent defect.

(3) (K, v) is called roughly deeply ramified (rdr) if:
   (DRvp) when char Kv = p > 0, the value v(p) is not the smallest positive element of vK; and
   (DRvr) when char Kv = p > 0, the ring O_{K̂}/pO_{K̂} is semiperfect, where K̂ denotes the completion of (K, v).

Question. Suppose (K, v) is a henselian valued field such that every algebraic extension of (K, v) is an independent defect field. Does it follow that (K, v) is roughly deeply ramified?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is presented as an explicit open problem in a recent survey on model theory of tame valued fields (December 2025). One direction—that every algebraic extension of a roughly deeply ramified field is an independent defect field—was established by Kuhlmann–Rzepka (2023). The converse, asked here, has not been established in the literature available; no resolution was located.
